items.stem: Define the term 'marketing'.
items.answer: The management process of identifying, anticipating and satisfying customer requirements profitably.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The management process of identifying, anticipating and satisfying customer requirements profitably. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between market orientation and product orientation.
items.answer: A market-oriented business finds out what customers want through research and then develops products to meet those needs; a product-oriented business develops products it thinks are good and then looks for customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark market orientation; 1 mark product orientation; 1 mark contrast/example. [3]

items.stem: Explain how marketing objectives are linked to corporate objectives.
items.answer: Marketing objectives are set to help achieve the corporate objectives; for example, a corporate objective of growth may lead to a marketing objective of raising sales by 15% in new markets.
items.markingKey: 1 mark derived from corporate objectives; 1 mark example. [2]

items.stem: Maple Learning is a private limited company in Toronto, Canada with about 260 staff. It runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students. Venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years. Explain how the marketing department could help Maple Learning achieve its corporate objectives.
items.answer: Points to develop for Maple Learning: marketing identifies and satisfies customer needs; market research guides product development such as a teacher-training platform for schools; promotion and pricing raise sales and market share; marketing objectives turn corporate aims into targets.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: marketing identifies and satisfies customer needs. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Maple Learning (education technology). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. market research guides product development such as a teacher-training platform for schools; promotion and pricing raise sales and market share. [3]

items.stem: Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Lagos Bites Ltd, a private limited company in Nigeria with about 700 employees, produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin. Explain the benefits to Lagos Bites of a market-oriented approach.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lagos Bites: market orientation bases decisions on customer needs; products such as packaged snacks match what customers want; higher sales and customer loyalty; early warning of changing tastes.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: market orientation bases decisions on customer needs. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Lagos Bites (food processing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. products such as packaged snacks match what customers want; higher sales and customer loyalty. [3]

items.stem: BatikPay Sdn Bhd is a private limited company based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops and employs about 210 people. The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. Discuss the importance of setting marketing objectives for BatikPay.
items.answer: For: provide focus and targets; coordinate the marketing mix; measure success. Against: objectives may be unrealistic; external changes; the marketing budget matters more. Judgement: for BatikPay it depends mainly on how the objectives link to corporate aims, and also on resources available.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (BatikPay: financial technology, about 210 employees, private limited company in Malaysia; the central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. provide focus and targets; coordinate the marketing mix; measure success; arguments against, e.g. objectives may be unrealistic; external changes; the marketing budget matters more. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how the objectives link to corporate aims; resources available; market conditions. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to BatikPay. [10]

items.stem: Explain why marketing must be coordinated with other departments.
items.answer: Marketing plans depend on operations to produce enough goods, finance to fund promotion and HR to provide trained staff; without coordination promises to customers cannot be met.
items.markingKey: 1 mark operations; 1 mark finance or HR; 1 mark consequence. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'demand'.
items.answer: The quantity of a product that consumers are willing and able to buy at each price in a given time period.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The quantity of a product that consumers are willing and able to buy at each price in a given time period. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two factors that could cause the demand for a product to increase.
items.answer: A rise in consumer incomes increases demand for normal goods; and a rise in the price of a substitute makes this product relatively cheaper, so more is bought.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark factor, 1 mark explanation): income, price of substitutes/complements, tastes, advertising, population. [4]

items.stem: Explain how a fall in supply affects the equilibrium price and quantity.
items.answer: The supply curve shifts left; at the original price there is excess demand, so the price rises until a new equilibrium is reached at a higher price and a lower quantity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark shift left; 1 mark excess demand at old price; 1 mark higher price, lower quantity. [3]

items.stem: IslaConnect Inc. is a private limited company based in Manila, the Philippines. It runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia and employs about 2,600 people. Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. Explain how a rise in the cost of raw materials could affect the market for call-centre and back-office services and IslaConnect.
items.answer: Points to develop for IslaConnect: supply falls when costs rise; the supply curve shifts left; the equilibrium price rises and quantity falls; the effect on revenue depends on how customers respond to price.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: supply falls when costs rise. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to IslaConnect (business process outsourcing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. the supply curve shifts left; the equilibrium price rises and quantity falls. [3]

items.answer: Points to develop for Lanka Tea: supply falls when costs rise; the supply curve shifts left; the equilibrium price rises and quantity falls; the effect on revenue depends on how customers respond to price.

Indus Sports Goods Ltd, a private limited company in Pakistan with about 950 employees, makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment. Identify and explain one advantage for Indus Sports of a sharp rise in demand for its footballs and cricket equipment.
items.answer: Higher sales and revenue; this would help Indus Sports, which makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. higher sales and revenue; can raise prices; better use of capacity. 1 mark: explained in the context of Indus Sports (sports equipment manufacturing). [2]

The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Explain the factors that could increase demand for Andes Textil's alpaca knitwear.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andes Textil: demand depends on price and other factors; rising incomes in Peru; changes in tastes and fashion; advertising and prices of substitutes.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: demand depends on price and other factors. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Andes Textil (textile manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. rising incomes in Peru; changes in tastes and fashion. [4]

items.stem: Define the term 'market size'.
items.answer: The total volume or value of sales in a market in a given period.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The total volume or value of sales in a market in a given period. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business could have rising sales but a falling market share.
items.answer: If the market is growing faster than the business's sales, its sales are a smaller percentage of the market, so its share falls even though sales rise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark market grows faster; 1 mark share = sales/market. [2]

items.stem: Explain two benefits to a business of being the market leader.
items.answer: Economies of scale lower costs; and retailers want to stock the leading brand, giving it more shelf space and bargaining power.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark benefit, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Lagos Bites Ltd is a private limited company based in Lagos, Nigeria. It produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin and employs about 700 people. Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Explain why market share is an important measure of performance for Lagos Bites.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lagos Bites: market share is sales as a percentage of the market; shows performance relative to rivals; a high share gives economies of scale; retailers and investors value market leaders.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: market share is sales as a percentage of the market. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Lagos Bites (food processing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. shows performance relative to rivals; a high share gives economies of scale. [3]

items.stem: The market for solar installations in Chile was worth $215m in 2024 and $223.6m in 2025. Sales of Andina Solar were $30.1m in 2024 and $30.7m in 2025. Calculate the market growth rate between 2024 and 2025.
Define the term 'mass marketing'.
items.answer: Selling the same product to the whole market with one marketing strategy.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Selling the same product to the whole market with one marketing strategy. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two benefits to a business of segmenting its market.
items.answer: It can design products and promotions that meet the needs of each group more precisely, raising sales; and it can identify gaps in the market and avoid wasting promotion on people unlikely to buy.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark benefit, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain one risk of niche marketing.
items.answer: The business depends on a small group of customers, so if their tastes change or a large rival enters the niche, sales may fall sharply.
items.markingKey: 1 mark risk; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Tanvir Textiles is a private limited company in Dhaka, Bangladesh with about 420 staff. It makes shirts and T-shirts for European fashion retailers. Labour turnover among machinists has risen sharply this year. Explain the benefits to Tanvir Textiles of targeting a niche market.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tanvir Textiles: niche marketing targets a small segment; less competition and higher prices; specialist image and loyalty; suits a business with limited resources.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: niche marketing targets a small segment. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Tanvir Textiles (clothing manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. less competition and higher prices; specialist image and loyalty. [3]

items.stem: Petra Prints Ltd is a private limited company based in Amman, Jordan. It prints leaflets, posters and packaging for local businesses and employs about 35 people. A large customer has started to pay its invoices late. Explain how Petra Prints could segment its market.
items.answer: Points to develop for Petra Prints: segmentation divides customers into groups; demographic segments such as age and income; geographic segments such as Jordan and Saudi Arabia; psychographic segments by lifestyle.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: segmentation divides customers into groups. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Petra Prints (printing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. demographic segments such as age and income; geographic segments such as Jordan and Saudi Arabia. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'consumer market'.
items.answer: A market for goods and services bought by individuals for their own use.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A market for goods and services bought by individuals for their own use. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Which is an example of an industrial market?
options: A café selling coffee
A steel company selling steel to a car manufacturer
A supermarket selling bread to shoppers
A cinema selling tickets
items.answer: A steel company selling steel to a car manufacturer
items.markingKey: A steel company selling steel to a car manufacturer. The buyer uses the steel in production. [1]

items.stem: Explain one difference between marketing to consumers and marketing to industrial buyers.
items.answer: Industrial buyers purchase in large quantities on technical specifications, price and reliability, so personal selling and relationships matter; consumer marketing uses mass advertising and branding to influence individual buyers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark industrial approach; 1 mark consumer approach. [2]

items.stem: Sales in its stores have fallen while online sales have grown. Atlas Furniture plc, a public limited company in Egypt with about 1,300 employees, makes furniture and sells it through 40 stores. Explain how Atlas Furniture could use customer relationship marketing to increase sales.
items.answer: Points to develop for Atlas Furniture: CRM builds long-term relationships; loyalty schemes encourage repeat purchases; personalised offers using customer data; excellent service and after-sales support.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: CRM builds long-term relationships. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Atlas Furniture (furniture manufacturing and retail). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. loyalty schemes encourage repeat purchases; personalised offers using customer data. [3]

items.stem: Nile Pharma plc is a public limited company based in Cairo, Egypt. It manufactures generic medicines for hospitals and pharmacies in Africa and the Middle East and employs about 1,800 people. Most of its raw ingredients are imported and paid for in US dollars. Evaluate whether customer relationship marketing is worthwhile for Nile Pharma.
items.answer: For: loyalty and repeat sales; lower cost than new customers; useful data. Against: costs of technology and staff; customers may still switch; privacy concerns. Judgement: for Nile Pharma it depends mainly on how competitive the market is, and also on the value of repeat customers.
